ledger.note: 504: Yiyang falls to the Wei. 'Liang lost the important border city Yiyang' (fall 504). Read as the Xinyang country (the northern-wei dossier places it with Hanzhong in 505).
505: Nanzheng and Hanzhong go to the Wei. 'in spring 505, the general Xiahou Daoqian rebelled and surrendered another important border city, Nanzheng,' to Northern Wei.
506: Wei Rui takes Hefei. 'In spring 506, the general Wei Rui was able to capture Hefei.' The Cliopatria shape already counts Hefei as Liang land; the pages do not say when the Wei had taken it.

ledger.note: 507: the Wei are beaten at Zhongli. They 'were defeated by a Liang army commanded by Wei and Cao Jingzong in spring 507'. The Huai front holds; Xinyang and Hanzhong stay Wei.
525: Pengcheng is surrendered to Liang. Northern Wei general Yuan Faseng surrendered it in spring 525.
525: Pengcheng is given back. Xiao Zong in summer 525 'in turn surrendered Pengcheng to Northern Wei, ending Liang's advances in the northeast.'
526: Shouyang falls to Liang. 'Shouyang fell to Liang troops after Emperor Wu successfully reemployed the damming strategy' (summer 526). Pei Shuye had surrendered it to the Wei in 500.

529: Liang's client Yuan Hao takes Luoyang. Yuan Hao was made Prince of Wei in winter 528; 'Emperor Xiaozhuang of Northern Wei fled the Northern Wei capital Luoyang, and Yuan Hao took it'. Chen Qingzhi captured Suiyang in spring 529. A client for weeks, not Liang land.
529: Luoyang is lost again. 'Luoyang later fell to Erzhu Rong's counterattack, and Chen fled back to Liang.' The page gives no month.
535: Lan Qin conquers Hanzhong. 'Lan Qin conquered Hanzhong, and forced the Western Wei to sue for peace.'

ledger.note: 544: Lý Bôn proclaims himself emperor in Jiaozhou. 'In 541, the Vietnamese people of Jiao Province ... declared a rebellion, led by Lý Bôn'; he 'declared himself emperor of Vietnam in 544'. The Early Lý dossier has the founding in 544.

Eastern Wei crushed the Henan base by 548 (Hanshan; Xiao Yuanming was captured).

region.text: the 13 provinces that Hou Jing commanded south of the Yellow River

ledger.note: 548: Hou Jing rebels against Liang. 'In spring 548, Hou's troops collapsed, and he approached Shouyang.' 'Hou declared a rebellion in summer 548' (Hou Jing page).
548: Hou Jing's rebellion reaches the capital. 'In winter 548, he arrived at Jiankang and immediately put the capital under siege.'
548: Hou Jing takes Shouyang by ambush. 'Southern Yu Province: he took its capital, Shouyang (modern central Anhui), in 548 by ambush.'
549: Jiankang falls to Hou Jing. 'Hou now had control of the capital region'; the Wu page: 'In late spring 549, the palace fell to Hou's troops'; Emperor Wu died in summer 549 (12 June Julian).
549: Hou Jing holds Zhejiang. 'by winter 549, Xiao Dalian and the other officials had fallen, which allowed Hou to control most of modern Zhejiang.'

ledger.note: 549: the northeast beyond the Yangtze submits to Eastern Wei. 'the northeastern provinces, north of the Yangtze River, largely surrendered to Eastern Wei' after Jiankang fell; 'Xiao Fan gave up Hefei to Eastern Wei'. No month on the page; the extent is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Xiangyang and the land north of the Han River

ledger.note: 550: Xiangyang goes to the Western Wei's side. Liang lost the land north of the Han River in 'spring 550', when Yang Zhong's forces, assisting Xiao Cha, took it; the Hou Jing page: Xiao Cha surrendered and 'Western Wei put Xiangyang under its protection'.

region.text: Jiaozhou, the Vietnamese province of Jiao Province

ledger.note: 550: Liang forces leave the Vietnamese lowlands. Liang forces 'would not be driven out until 550'.
552: Hou Jing is destroyed. He died c. 26 May 552; 'Wang Sengbian cut off the head and delivered it to Xiao Yi'; Chen Baxian defeated him at Jiankang. The capital region and Zhejiang return to Liang.

552: Xiao Ji claims the throne in Yi Province. The infobox lists him as a pretender 'from 16 May 552 to 5 August 553'; he claimed the throne 'around the same time' Hou Jing was defeated. This page does not name Sichuan as his base; the Xiao Ji page (opened for xiao-ji-s-rebel-state) says he 'governed the modern Sichuan and Chongqing region' and 'declared himself emperor in spring 552'. 'Western Wei captured Xiao Ji's domain' in 553.

region.text: the capital region and most of Zhejiang

ledger.note: 552: Zhejiang and the capital region return to Liang. 'Chen defeated him as well'; Wang Sengbian sent Hou Jing's head to Xiao Yi.
552: Xiao Yi takes the imperial title and stays at Jiangling. 'In winter 552, Xiao Yi finally took imperial title (as Emperor Yuan)'; 'For the time being, the capital was at Jiangling.'

553: Hanzhong goes to the Western Wei with Sichuan. Every page opened is silent on Hanzhong; the year follows the Western Wei's conquest of Xiao Ji's domain ('Meanwhile, Western Wei captured Xiao Ji's domain, and that territory would be permanently lost'), and Cliopatria hands Hanzhong with Chengdu to the Western Wei.

555: the Liang court is at Jiankang again under Wang Sengbian. Infobox 'Jiankang (502-552, 555-557)'; 'Liang generals led by Wang Sengbian declared' Xiao Fangzhi emperor at Jiankang; Northern Qi then defeated them (Liang page).

555: Western Wei sacks Jiangling, kills Emperor Yuan and sets up Xiao Cha. 'In winter 554, Yuwen Tai launched his attack'; 'In January 555, Western Wei forces put Emperor Yuan to death'; the Liang page: 'in 555, Western Wei army sacked Jiangling'.

wars.name: Hou Jing's rebellion
wars.outcome: Hou Jing defects in 547, rebels in summer 548, takes Jiankang in spring 549 and proclaims the Han in November 551; Chen Baxian and Wang Sengbian destroy him in May 552.

wars.name: Xiao Yi's war with Xiao Ji and the Western Wei conquest of Yi Province
wars.outcome: Xiao Yi has Xiao Ji put to death; the Western Wei capture his domain, 'permanently lost' to Liang.

wars.name: Western Wei conquest of Jiangling
wars.outcome: Yuwen Tai's attack of winter 554 takes Jiangling; Emperor Yuan is put to death in January 555 and Xiao Cha set up.
wars.note: The Liang page also has Northern Qi attacking Liang in 553 ('In 553, Northern Qi attacked Liang'); no outcome and no land on either page.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line on any page opened. The Huai, Han and Yangtze fronts and the Jiaozhou frontier are approximate; the lost cities are drawn as discs round the places the pages name.

sources.title: Liang dynasty
sources.note: Identity, dates (30 April 502 - 16 November 557), capitals, emperors, the Hou Jing years, 553-555, successors. Infobox gives no area.

sources.title: Emperor Wu of Liang
sources.note: 503-507, 525-529 and 535 wars, Jiaozhou 541-550, Hou Jing's rebellion in summer 548. Silent on Linyi, the Hephthalites and the Tuyuhun.

sources.title: Hou Jing
sources.note: 547 defection, 548-552 rebellion, Shouyang, Zhejiang, the northeast lost to Eastern Wei, Hou's death c. 26 May 552.

sources.title: Emperor Yuan of Liang
sources.note: Jiangling 552-555, Xiao Ji 552-553, the Western Wei conquest of Yi Province, the sack of Jiangling January 555, Xiangyang 550.

sources.title: Western Wei
sources.note: Fifth page. Thin: 'occupied the territory of modern Sichuan' (undated); Western Wei ended 14 February 557.

notes: Cliopatria rows: 'Liang Dynasty' 510-560 is the Southern Liang (502-557), not the Later Liang of the Five Dynasties: the two rows share Wikidata Q783489 but are different states (the Later Liang is 907-923, dossier later-liang-dynasty by another group); the wikidata field keeps Cliopatria's value, unverified. The Cliopatria shapes: (1) start eight years late and end three years late; (2) keep Xinyang, Hanzhong and Shouyang throughout; (3) hand Sichuan and Hanzhong to the Western Wei in 536, seventeen years before the pages (553; the Emperor Yuan page); (4) drop Vietnam in 546 although the Wu page keeps Liang forces there to 550; (5) hold the provinces north of the Yangtze, Xiangyang and Zhejiang after the Hou Jing war; (6) run a 1.94 M km2 shape to 560 although the court was reduced to Jiankang's neighbourhood by 555 and the empire ended in November 557. All are repaired with new keyframes 502-553 and the three wrong verdicts. NOT SETTLED: (a) dates of the Wei losses of Hefei and Shouyang before 506 and 526 (pages silent); whether Xinyang was ever recovered; (b) the date of Hanzhong's fall (confidence 1); (c) Linyi (Champa) recognised by Liang in 530 (Lâm Ấp page, not opened here; the champa dossier decides); (d) Funan, Baekje, Silla, the Hephthalites and the Tuyuhun: the pages opened are silent, so no vassal events; (e) the extents of 'the northeastern provinces north of the Yangtze' and 'most of Zhejiang' are the researcher's readings (Anhui and Jiangsu minus Jiangnan; Zhejiang); (f) Xiao Ji's pretender state in Sichuan (552-553, about fifteen months) has no dossier: counterpart 'xiao-ji-s-rebel-state' needs one; Hou Jing's rebel state is written here as hou-jing-s-han. (g) The Western Wei page was thin; the Hanzhong and Sichuan dates need another page (Yuwen Tai's biography).
